final_report.rationale: The incident narrative describes a failure to detect ventricular fibrillation (VF), a life-threatening arrhythmia, which constitutes a serious potential patient-safety risk in a safety-critical function. Although the specific episode self-resolved with no recorded adverse outcome and recurrence is not yet confirmed, the nature of VF detection failures inherently carries high severity due to the potential for death or serious harm if the event had persisted longer or occurred without spontaneous resolution (Severity 3 criteria). The missing confidence-score log prevents a complete technical root-cause analysis and validation of whether this was an algorithmic failure or a logging defect. This gap, combined with the safety-critical nature of the missed detection, triggers obligations under EU MDR Annex I Section 3 regarding risk management updates based on post-market surveillance data (mdr-annexI-sec3-risk-management-system) and FDA QMSR requirements for complaint records including details of the failure (qmsr-820.35-records). No relevant technical artifacts (code diffs, test logs, or specific deployment logs for this device instance) were retrieved to confirm the root cause; all retrieved static analysis outputs are explicitly labeled as unrelated distractors.
